summary: Two-layer liveness protection: supervised-run.sh enforces hard process-group deadlines for killable subprocesses (confirmed active in production telemetry); schedule-hang-check.sh/hang-check.sh schedule a metrics-derived one-shot stall detector for native-agent stalls that has never been observed to fire outside tests.

entry_points.summary: Schedules schedule-hang-check.sh after successful registry registration when watchdog and registry are enabled.
Schedules a one-shot hang-check at a metrics-derived horizon; no daemon teardown required.
Hard-deadline wrapper for external commands; emits dispatch leases and watchdog_timeout on enforced deadline.
Computes per-class threshold seconds from historical wall_ms p90/p95 times margin; sparse fallback to watchdog.stale_secs.
Schedules self-removing launchd one-shot or detached fallback for hang-check.sh; emits no scheduling telemetry.
One-shot liveness check; exits 0; notifies once (watchdog_stall) only when stale unmatched starts remain.
Read-only unmatched *_start inspector with stale threshold and lifecycle deny-list.
Best-effort Discord/macOS alert path for watchdog_stall and watchdog_timeout, gated by notify.level.
Resolve timeout, gtimeout, or bash_fallback backend; header still mentions retired watchdog-sweep.sh.
watchdog.enabled (default true), stale_secs, kill_grace_secs, intervention_level, timeout_secs.*.
Legacy pid-file cleanup during deregister; best-effort and non-fatal.
Only self-referenced; no importers found. Superseded by scripts/hermes/mcp-hermes-orchestrator.py.
External reviewer provider calls are wrapped in supervised-run.
rsync/cargo/ssh remote operations run under supervised-run and emit orphan hints on timeout.

invariants: Killable subprocesses can be killed and routed to retry/halt; native Agent stalls can only be detected and alerted.
dispatch_id pairs dispatch start/end events; matching must not rely only on type or pid.
supervised-run.sh preserves child stdout and writes its own diagnostics to stderr.
Exit code 124 means the wrapper enforced a deadline.
Watchdog telemetry and notification are fail-open; failure must not prevent the wrapped command or scheduled check from completing.
Scheduled hang-check exits 0 even on detection/evaluation issues; it must not fail loudly.
Notify-once markers prevent repeated alerts for the same run/reason.
watchdog.timeout_secs.* is config-file-only and read via config.py get, not env-exported.
notify.level defaults to approval_only and watchdog_stall/watchdog_timeout are in the approval_only fire-set (since commit e6c54a0, 2026-06-19).
gotchas: Old watchdog-sweep.sh/watchdog-spawn.sh daemon scripts are gone from the tree; do not document them as live paths.
schedule-hang-check.sh emits no scheduling telemetry event, so 0 watchdog_stall events in history does not distinguish never-scheduled from scheduled-but-never-stale.

As of this refresh: 0 watchdog_stall events found anywhere in local .local/state/z-harness run history (all repos, all runs); Layer 1 (supervised-run) has 124+ real dispatch pairs and confirmed real (non-test) watchdog_timeout firings.
The 2026-06-21 'notify.level=off' root cause for Layer 2 silence is stale — fixed 2026-06-19 in commit e6c54a0; current silence is unexplained by config, not a known misconfiguration.
liveness.sh ignores broad lifecycle brackets and focuses on subagent/action starts with matching ends.
hang-threshold.py class keys depend on event fields that actually exist (persona_attempt_outcome role/tier, subagent_model, or kind).
Remote command timeouts may leave a remote systemd-run unit alive; remote-runner emits remote_orphan_possible guidance.
scripts/hermes/watchdog_webhook.py is dead code (no importers); do not treat as live Discord so integration.
check-timeout.sh header comments still reference watchdog-sweep.sh as a caller; stale comment, not a real dependency.
